name: Puka Nacua

background.fact: Born May 29, 2001 (Wikipedia says Las Vegas, Nevada); grew up in Provo, Utah and attended Orem High School, finishing with 260 receptions, 5,226 yards and 58 touchdowns, all Utah state records.
His mother is of Samoan and German descent and his father was of Hawaiian and Portuguese descent. The nickname Puka is Samoan for fat and chubby, given because of his size as a baby.
He played college football at Washington and then BYU, and the Rams took him in the fifth round (pick 177) of the 2023 draft.

As a rookie he set NFL rookie records for receiving yards and receptions (105 for 1,486), made the Pro Bowl and second-team All-Pro; in 2025 he led the league in receptions (129 for 1,715 and 10 touchdowns) and was first-team All-Pro.
Listed 6 ft 2 in, 216 lb, age 25, jersey 12, fourth NFL season.

family.fact: Wikipedia says he has one son, born in October 2025, with his college girlfriend Hallie. Nothing further about the child is recorded here.

Older brothers Samson (receiver, Michigan Panthers of the UFL) and Kai (safety, Michigan Panthers, formerly in the NFL) both play pro football; cousin Marist Liufau is a linebacker for the Dallas Cowboys.
His father, Lionel, died of complications from diabetes when Puka was 11.

scouts_read: Nacua will not play at Arizona, so this is a roster hole, not a matchup question. He went on injured reserve with knee ligament sprains and turf toe, which means at least four games out and a realistic return no earlier than Week 15, with turf toe the injury most likely to drag. Before the injury he was the Rams' engine, averaging 14.8 points with a 14 catch, 150 yard game in his last outing. With Adams also on IR, the Rams passing targets spread to depth receivers, which makes any single replacement risky. For fantasy purposes, count him as zero until his return is confirmed.
